connector.tooTall: A lift reaches up to 48 m: in the game you need to chain two or use floor holes.
connector.ports: The bottom port is shown on floor {{bottom}} and the top one on floor {{top}}.

power.title: Plan power
power.infiniteOn: Assumes there is a grid able to power the whole plan: no need to run power lines. Any lines you draw count as connected to that grid.
power.infiniteOff: Every machine must be wired to a grid with generators, or to a pole hooked up to your world grid.
power.worldHint: You can read them in game on any power pole or in the power panel. Do not include this plan.
power.enough: Enough: with the plan built you have {{mw}} MW left.
power.notEnough: Not enough: {{mw}} MW short. You need more generators before building this.
power.fillWorld: Enter your world production and consumption to see whether it is enough.
power.trainsNote: Includes {{mw}} MW from locomotives (110 MW each, the most they draw when accelerating).

palette.pathHint: Click a port or the ground to start and click again to finish the segment.
palette.consumptionRange: Consumption: {{min}} to {{max}} MW depending on the recipe and the point in the cycle

community.title: Community
community.guestHint: You can view plans without an account. Sign in to share your own.
community.empty: No shared plans yet. Share one from My plans.
community.emptyQuery: No shared plans with that name yet. Share one from My plans.

production.bottleneck: Producing at {{pct}} of ideal: each cycle takes {{actual}} s instead of {{ideal}} s waiting for {{item}}.
production.outputLimited: The output cannot take everything it could produce: the belt is at capacity or what follows consumes less. The rest builds up in the machine.
production.adviceUnder: Downstream needs less: with the clock at {{pct}} it makes exactly what is needed and uses less power.
production.adviceOver: Not enough for what downstream needs: set the clock to {{pct}}.
production.adviceOverClock: Not enough for what downstream needs: set the clock to {{pct}} (overclock: {{shards}} power shard(s)) or add one more machine.
production.adviceImpossible: Not even 250 % is enough: downstream needs the equivalent of {{pct}}. You need {{machines}} machines at 100 % (or {{max}} at 250 %).

splitter.help: Each output lets through what its filter says. Any Undefined takes the items no other output names and Overflow gets what does not fit in the others.

merger.help: What the output needs is taken first from the inputs with the highest priority (1).

storage.capacityFluid: Capacity: {{n}} m³. Works as a buffer: it absorbs differences in rate between what goes in and what comes out.
storage.capacitySlots: Capacity: {{n}} slots. Works as a buffer: it absorbs differences in rate between what goes in and what comes out.
storage.connect: Connect belts or pipes to see how long it takes to fill.
storage.fills: Fills up in {{time}}; then it backs up the input.
storage.empties: Empties in {{time}} if it starts full.
storage.steady: As much goes in as comes out: the level holds.

route.distanceHint: Empty: the drawn path or, with no waypoints, the straight line + 20 % (drones fly straight). Type a value to use the real distance you measured in the game.
route.roundTrip: Round trip: {{t}} s ({{dist}} m of travel + {{dock}} s loading and unloading).
route.genericCapacity: {{n}}/min for items that stack to 100. Connect belts to the origin station to see the real item.

source.drawn_one: Distance of the drawn path (1 waypoint).
source.drawn_other: Distance of the drawn path ({{count}} waypoints).
source.droneStraight: Drones fly in a straight line.

route.drawHelp: With the route selected: drag a point to move it, double-click the path to add one and double-click a point to remove it.
route.fuelTrip: {{n}} per round trip · {{m}}/min for the whole route
route.fuelElectric: Trains are electric: the locomotive draws 25 to 110 MW from the grid.
route.fuelDrone: Per trip: 24,000 MJ plus 6 MJ per meter. Speed depends on the fuel.

side.buildingHelp: Rotation {{rot}}° · <kbd>R</kbd> rotate · right-click or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to exit
side.drawingHelpBelt: Capacity {{cap}}. Click a port (or the ground, which places a pole) to start and click again to finish. If you finish on the ground, drawing continues from there. Up to 56 m per segment.
side.drawingHelpPipe: Capacity {{cap}}. Click a port (or the ground, which places a support) to start and click again to finish. If you finish on the ground, drawing continues from there. Up to 56 m per segment.
side.createRoute: Create a route from this station
side.selectionHelp: <kbd>R</kbd> rotate · <kbd>Del</kbd> delete · <kbd>Ctrl+X</kbd> move · <kbd>Ctrl+C</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl+V</kbd> copy · right-click: options
side.wholePlanSummary: {{structures}} buildings · {{segments}} segments. Drag over the plan to select an area and see its materials.
side.controlsView: Wheel: zoom · Middle button or <kbd>Space</kbd>+drag: pan · <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>/<kbd>Y</kbd>: undo/redo · <kbd>Shift</kbd>+click or box: add to selection (you can pan in between) · <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+box: remove · <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd>: whole floor · dragging the box to the edge pans the view · right-click: options
side.controlsBuild: Foundations: drag to fill an area · click the loose end of a belt or pipe: keep drawing it
side.drawingHelpHyper: Click a hypertube entrance, junction or floor hole (or the ground, which places a support) to start and click again to finish. If you finish on the ground, drawing continues from there. Up to 100 m per segment; it costs its materials for every meter.
side.poleHeightHint: Machines send and receive belts at 1 m. Between two different heights the belt climbs on a slope, which cannot exceed 35°. If it runs higher than a machine, it passes over without colliding.

machine.overclock: Overclock: needs {{n}} power shard(s). Use it only if there is no alternative.
machine.somersloopsHelp: Produces +{{pct}} % from the same inputs; power usage is multiplied by {{mult}}.
machine.outputSlack: What is connected downstream does not consume everything it produces.
machine.inputShort: Not enough material arrives to run at 100 %.
machine.underclockHint: Lowering the clock to {{pct}} runs it with no waste.
machine.variablePower: Variable consumption: between {{min}} and {{max}} MW over each cycle. The grid counts the average, {{avg}} MW.

calc.title: Production calculator
calc.searchPlaceholder: What do you want to make… (e.g. Modular Frame)
calc.onlyUnlocked: Only recipes unlocked in my progress
calc.splitFull: At 100 % plus one with the rest
calc.intro: Search for a product, enter how many you want per minute and I will build the whole chain down to the raw resources.
calc.heading: {{rate}} {{item}} per minute
calc.colImportTitle: Do not make it here: you bring it from elsewhere
calc.byproductsHelp: They must be taken out (stored, used or sent to the AWESOME Sink) or the machine stops.
calc.wireSummary: With connections: {{segments}} segments ({{meters}} m) with mergers, splitters and pipeline junctions in manifolds. The miners and extractors go at the bottom, with the best tier you have unlocked and the exact clock, and the final product exits to the right. Where two lines cross, in the game one goes over the other on a taller pole.
calc.placeHint: It is placed to the right of what you already have, with recipes and clocks set.
calc.minersOre: Miners Mk.1 on a normal node

build.beltShort: {{item}}: {{rate}}/min exceeds the fastest belt available; consider splitting it into two lines.
build.pipeShort: {{item}}: {{rate}}/min exceeds the fastest pipeline available; consider splitting it into two lines.
build.miners: Miners and extractors sized for normal nodes at the exact clock; in the game each goes on its own node: if yours is pure or impure, change the purity on the miner and the app recalculates.
build.byproduct: Byproduct: {{item}} ({{rate}}/min) exits to the right; store it, use it or send it to the AWESOME Sink so the machine does not stop.
build.looseBelt: {{item}}: comes in through a loose pole at the bottom; connect whatever brings it there.
build.loosePipe: {{item}}: comes in through a loose support at the bottom; connect whatever brings it there.
build.skippedFluids: {{n}} fluid output(s) with no port to connect.
build.crossings_one: 1 line crossing remains: in the game you get past it by lifting one line over the other or using another floor.
build.crossings_other: {{count}} line crossings remain: in the game you get past them by lifting one line over the other or using another floor.
build.byproductSink: By-product: {{item}} ({{rate}}/min) goes to the AWESOME Sink, which turns it into coupon points.
build.byproductStorage: By-product: {{item}} ({{rate}}/min) goes to a {{place}}, which fills up in {{time}}; then the machine stops.
build.byproductFluidTank: By-product: {{item}} ({{rate}}/min) is a fluid and cannot go into the AWESOME Sink: it goes to a {{place}}, which fills up in {{time}}. To get rid of it, package it and send the packages to the Sink.
build.power: Power: {{poles}} poles ({{pole}}) and {{wires}} wires. The first pole is connected to the world grid.
build.powerFar: Some power line is longer than 100 m: check the wires marked in red.

problems.title: Plan problems
problems.allGood: No problems: everything can be built like this in the game.
problems.hint: Click a problem to go there: it switches floor, selects it and centers it.
problems.checks: Checked: overlapping structures, belts and pipes going through structures, segments that are too long, belt slope (35° max), wires over 100 m and poles with more wires than they allow. With the real map, also miners and extractors that are not on their node.
problems.through: {{a}} goes through {{b}}: route around it, or lift it with poles taller than the structure.
problems.tooLong: {{a}} is {{n}} m long and the maximum is {{max}} m: add a pole or support in the middle.
problems.slope: {{a}} climbs at {{n}}° and the maximum is 35°: move the poles further apart or use a conveyor lift.
problems.wireLong: A wire is {{n}} m long and the maximum is {{max}} m: add a pole in the middle.
problems.poleFull: {{a}} has {{n}} wires and allows {{max}}: add another pole or use one with more connections.
problems.trainNoTrack: A train goes from {{a}} to {{b}}, but no track connects them.
problems.trainsNoSignals: {{n}} trains share this track without signals: they will crash. Place block signals to split the network.
problems.offNode: {{a}} is not on a suitable resource node
problems.nodeMismatch: {{a}}: the node below is {{purity}} {{item}}; adjust the resource or purity
problems.designerOutside: {{a}} sticks out of the build area of the {{b}}

train.title: Train with timetable
train.trainsHint: Several trains can run the same timetable; if they share track they need signals.
train.length: Train length: {{m}} m (each locomotive and each car is 16 m). With more than one locomotive, put the extra ones at the back: cars are counted from the first one.
train.noPlatforms: No platforms: the train stops but does not load or unload.
train.fewPlatforms: Cars {{n}} to {{wagons}} have no platform at this station.
train.cycle: Full loop: {{m}} m in {{s}} s, with {{dock}} s of docking at each of the {{stops}} stops.
train.platformHelp: Each car uses the platform at its position: car 1 uses the first platform after the station. Select a platform to choose whether it loads or unloads.
train.powerUse: Between {{min}} and {{max}} MW: {{n}} locomotives at 25 to 110 MW each, depending on load and slope. The plan's power counts the maximum, on the grid of its stations.
train.nothingYet: Nothing reaches the loading platforms yet.
train.noLoads: No car has both a loading and an unloading platform along the route.
train.noPlatformsHelp: No platforms: attach them in a row to one end of the station, one per car.
train.platformLoose: It is not attached to any station: place it in a row next to a station or another platform.
train.missingTrack: Track is missing between some stops.

blocks.empty: You have not saved any blocks yet.
blocks.designer: Fits in the Blueprint Designer Mk.{{n}}

blocks.name: Name

map.title: Real map
map.intro: Place the plan on the game map: you see the terrain in the background and the real resource nodes with their purity, and each miner snaps onto its node.
map.at: Plan origin at game X {{x}} m, Y {{y}} m · grid rotated {{angle}}°
map.snapHelp: When you place a miner, oil extractor, well extractor, pressurizer or geothermal generator near a node, it snaps on top and takes the node's resource and purity.
map.source: Nodes taken from the game (version 1.2, standard world: they do not match game modes that shuffle nodes). Map image: official wiki.
map.pickTitle: Place the plan on the map
map.pickHelp: Click on the map where you want to build: the plan appears centered there. Wheel: zoom · drag the map: pan.
map.angleHelp: In the game the foundation grid follows the first foundation you place, at any angle. Rotate it until it matches your save.
map.dragHelp: Drag the plan to move it and the round handle to rotate it around its center (with Shift, in 15° steps). A click elsewhere on the map moves it there.
map.handleLegend: rotation handle, on the plan north side

augmenter.help: Generates {{mw}} MW and increases all generation on its grid by {{base}} % (other generators too, and the world grid if it is linked). With {{rate}} Alien Power Matrices per minute the boost goes up to {{fueled}} %. Boosts from several augmenters add up.
augmenter.fueled: Receives {{rate}} matrices per minute (no belt in the plan)
augmenter.infinite: Infinite power: the plan adds +{{pct}} % to the whole grid
augmenter.noGrid: No wires: it boosts no grid. Connect it with a wire to the grid you want to boost.

battery.help: Stores {{mwh}} MWh. It charges with the spare power on its grid, up to {{mw}} MW, and when generation falls short it supplies the difference, with no limit, until it runs empty; then the grid trips.
battery.infinite: With infinite power the grid always has enough: the storage stays full.
battery.noGrid: No wires: connect it with a wire to the grid you want to back up.
battery.draining: {{mw}} MW short: when full, they last {{time}} and then the grid trips.
battery.idle: Generation and consumption are even: they neither charge nor discharge.
battery.peaks: At the peak of variable-power machines up to {{mw}} MW is missing: the storage covers those moments.

switch.help: Joins the grids on its two sides when on; when off, they stay separate and each one runs on its own generation.
switch.helpPriority: Joins the grids on its two sides. If power falls short (and the storage is empty), it cuts off on its own by group, before the whole grid trips.
switch.autoOff: Cut off on its own: with everything on, the grid cannot power its consumption.
switch.groupHelp: When power runs short, undefined switches cut first, then groups 8 to 1. Put in group 1 whatever cannot stop, like what makes fuel for the generators.
switch.gameNote: In the game switches are placed off; here they start on so the grid stays joined while you plan.

valve.help: Limits the pipe flow rate. It has an input and an output: fluid goes from the input to the output.

designer.help: You can only build inside the marked area: {{m}} × {{m}} m ({{n}} × {{n}} foundations) and {{m}} m tall. What you build there is saved as a blueprint in the game; here you can save it as a block.
designer.outside_one: {{count}} structure sticks out of the area: the game would not allow it.
designer.outside_other: {{count}} structures stick out of the area: the game would not allow them.

monitor.noBeltLong: It is not on a belt: place it on one to measure it.
